nodes.label:
Warm up iron in stand,
ventilate the area
nodes.title: Warm up iron in stand, ventilate the area
nodes.info: The iron goes into its stand before it is plugged in, never on the bench. Open a window or run a fan so solder fumes move away from the person leaning over the joint.

nodes.label:
Iron touches
only the joint
nodes.title: Iron touches only the joint
nodes.info: Heat the pad and the lead together for a couple of seconds, then feed solder to the joint -- not to the iron tip. Nothing else on the bench should ever be touched with the tip.

nodes.label:
Return iron to the
stand immediately
nodes.title: Return iron to the stand immediately
nodes.info: The iron goes back in the stand between every joint, without exception. A hot iron resting on the bench is how burns and scorched cables happen in a busy room.

nodes.label:
Wait 10 seconds
before touching the joint
nodes.title: Wait 10 seconds before touching the joint
nodes.info: A finished joint stays hot enough to burn for several seconds after the iron leaves it. Count to ten before handling the board or tugging the wire to test it.

nodes.label:
Iron off and cooled
before storage
nodes.title: Iron off and cooled before storage
nodes.info: Switch off at the wall, leave the iron in its stand, and let it cool fully before it goes back in the box. A hot iron packed away is a fire in a cupboard.
